title: Role opening → ramped hire
description: Run capacity justification, sourcing, and onboarding design as one ordered pipeline, focusing the ramp-plan phase where the real design work happens.
yaml:
apiVersion: ladder.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Workflow
metadata:
  name: wf-hr-02
  title: Role opening → ramped hire
  description: Run capacity justification, sourcing, and onboarding design as one ordered pipeline, focusing
    the ramp-plan phase where the real design work happens.
  version: 1.0.0
spec:
  objective: Take an approved opening through to a day-90 ramp plan with observable checkpoints and a
    named owner for every dependency.
  policies:
    maxConcurrency: 4
    onFailure: preserve-completed
    requireApprovalFor:
      - n-approval
  nodes:
    - id: n-intake
      kind: input
      name: Opening request and team context
      summary: Opening request and team context
      inputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - text
        properties:
          text:
            type: string
            description: The requester's objective, source material, or instructions.
          workflowFields:
            type: object
            required:
              - role_scorecard
              - committed_demand
              - team_composition
              - start_date
            properties:
              role_scorecard: {}
              committed_demand: {}
              team_composition: {}
              start_date: {}
        x-ladder-input-mode: text
    - id: n-phase1
      kind: agent
      templateRef: hr-05
      name: Capacity justification for the opening
      summary: 'Phase 1: capacity justification for the opening.'
      role: Workforce planner modeling headcount, attrition, and skill supply against committed demand.
      prompt: You are a Workforce Capacity Planner. You model required capacity by skill and level against
        committed demand, using explicit attrition, hiring-funnel yield, and ramp-time assumptions, and
        you show which assumption the plan is most sensitive to. You state ramp time as a real cost —
        a headcount plan that treats a new hire as fully productive on day one is a staffing shortfall
        with a start date.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - simulation
          - decision-analysis
          - statistical-analysis
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors:
          - mcp:hris
          - mcp:data-warehouse
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n-phase2
      kind: agent
      templateRef: hr-01
      name: Evidence-backed candidate pool
      summary: 'Phase 2: evidence-backed candidate pool.'
      role: Sourcing researcher building evidence-backed candidate pools against a written role scorecard.
      prompt: You are a Talent Sourcing Researcher. You translate a role scorecard into searchable signals
        and build a candidate pool where every inclusion cites the specific public evidence that matched,
        so a reviewer can check the reasoning rather than trust the ranking. You avoid proxies that stand
        in for protected characteristics — school prestige, career-gap penalties, name-based inference
        — and say when the pool is too narrow to be fair.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - supply-chain-analysis
          - writing-editing
          - evidence-verification
          - source-triangulation
        tools:
          - read
          - search
        connectors:
          - mcp:ats
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n-phase3
      kind: agent
      templateRef: hr-06
      name: Compensation band placement
      summary: 'Phase 3: compensation band placement.'
      role: Compensation analyst placing roles in bands against market data and internal equity.
      prompt: You are a Compensation Band Analyst. You place a role against survey benchmarks with the
        survey, cut, and effective date named, then test the placement against internal equity for comparable
        scope. You surface compression and equity outliers you were not asked about, because an offer
        that fixes one candidate and breaks three tenured employees is not a solved problem.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - domain-analysis
          - design-review
          - statistical-analysis
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors:
          - mcp:hris
        permissions:
          - pii-restricted
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n-stages
      kind: group
      name: Opening preparation
      summary: Each phase consumes the previous phase's output; the group exits only after every phase
        result has been serialized in order.
      config:
        members:
          - n-phase1
          - n-phase2
          - n-phase3
        execution: sequential
        exit: serialize
    - id: n-focus
      kind: subgraph
      name: Ramp plan design
      summary: The 30/60/90 design phase, focused on the canvas because this is where the checkpoints,
        access dependencies, and owners are actually decided.
    - id: n-check
      kind: evaluate
      inlineRole: true
      name: Check the staged result
      summary: Evaluate checkpoint observability, dependency ownership, and access lead times against
        the start date.
      role: Deterministic metric evaluator
      prompt: Evaluate the upstream result against checkpoint observability, dependency ownership, and
        access lead times against the start date. Return a score, pass/fail verdict, the evidence behind
        the verdict, remaining uncertainty, and the smallest corrective action. Do not claim programmatic
        measurement unless the host supplies the required tool.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - evaluation
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - score
          - passed
          - reasons
        properties:
          score:
            type: number
          passed:
            type: boolean
          reasons:
            type: array
            items:
              type: string
      config:
        threshold: 0.8
    - id: n-ready
      kind: condition
      name: Ready to commit?
      summary: Route on check.passed.
      config:
        expression: check.passed
        branches:
          - label: Ready
            when: 'true'
          - label: Rework
            when: 'false'
    - id: n-rework
      kind: agent
      templateRef: hr-04
      name: Repair the ramp plan gaps
      summary: Smallest corrective pass before re-gating.
      role: Onboarding designer building role-specific ramp plans with observable checkpoints.
      prompt: You are an Onboarding Program Designer. You design a ramp plan backwards from what the person
        must be able to do independently by day 30, 60, and 90, with an observable checkpoint for each
        milestone and a named owner for every access, tool, and introduction. You flag dependencies that
        will silently block a new hire — an access request with a two-week SLA scheduled for day two is
        a plan that has already failed.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - design-review
          - domain-analysis
          - evaluation
        tools:
          - read
          - write
        connectors:
          - mcp:hris
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n-approval
      kind: approval
      name: People partner sign-off before the plan is committed
      summary: Pause for the people partner; on timeout, escalate.
    - id: workflow-output
      kind: output
      name: Released deliverable
      summary: Return the completed Role opening → ramped hire deliverable, the evidence behind it, and
        every unresolved item.
  edges:
    - id: wf-hr-02-edge-1
      from: n-intake
      to: n-stages
      kind: data
    - id: wf-hr-02-edge-2
      from: n-stages
      to: n-focus
      kind: data
    - id: wf-hr-02-edge-3
      from: n-focus
      to: n-check
      kind: data
    - id: wf-hr-02-edge-4
      from: n-check
      to: n-ready
      kind: data
    - id: wf-hr-02-edge-5
      from: n-ready
      to: n-approval
      kind: control
      condition: 'true'
    - id: wf-hr-02-edge-6
      from: n-ready
      to: n-rework
      kind: control
      condition: 'false'
    - id: wf-hr-02-edge-7
      from: n-rework
      to: n-approval
      kind: data
    - id: wf-hr-02-edge-8
      from: n-approval
      to: workflow-output
      kind: dependency
      condition: approved
